Build a Graphical Lasso Network (EBICglasso)

Source: R/estimate_network.R
build_glasso.Rd

build_glasso() estimates a regularised partial correlation network with the graphical lasso: an L1 penalty shrinks small partial correlations to exactly zero, and the penalty is chosen along a path of nlambda values by the extended Bayesian information criterion (EBIC; Foygel & Drton, 2010). It is build_network() with method = "glasso". The settings go in params: gamma (the EBIC hyperparameter, default 0.5; larger values give sparser networks), nlambda (default 100), lambda.min.ratio (default 0.01), penalize.diagonal (default FALSE), refit (default FALSE; TRUE re-estimates the selected edges without the penalty) and cor_method.

An absent edge means the penalty set it to zero at the selected lambda, not that the two variables are shown to be independent. Check the stability of the edges and centralities with boot_glasso().

Usage

build_glasso(data, actor = NULL, level = NULL, ...)

Arguments

data

The variables: a data frame with one row per observation and one column per variable, or a square symmetric correlation or covariance matrix, which needs the sample size in params (as in params = list(n = 250)). Non-numeric columns are set aside; a frame of two or more character or factor columns and fewer than two numeric ones is read as sequences and turned into per-row state counts first. A column named rid is set aside; columns with non-syntactic names, all-missing and constant columns, and rows with a missing value are dropped, each with a message; fewer than 2 variables or 3 complete rows raise an error.

actor

The id column naming whose observation each row is (a person). With level, the decomposition groups by it; without, it is set aside, not modelled. Default NULL.

level

Multilevel decomposition, with actor: "between" estimates the network of person means, "within" the network of deviations from them, and "both" returns the two as a netobject_ml. Default NULL (no decomposition).

...

Further arguments for build_network(), such as params (gamma, nlambda, refit, n and the others above), threshold, scaling or group. method cannot be given: it is always "glasso" (error of class nestimate_bad_input).

Value

A netobject (a netobject_group with group, a netobject_ml with level = "both"), exactly as build_network() returns it: print it for an overview, read the edges with extract_edges(), and draw it with cograph::splot().

References

Friedman, J., Hastie, T., & Tibshirani, R. (2008). Sparse inverse covariance estimation with the graphical lasso. Biostatistics, 9(3), 432–441. doi:10.1093/biostatistics/kxm045

Foygel, R., & Drton, M. (2010). Extended Bayesian information criteria for Gaussian graphical models. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 23, 604–612.

See also

build_network

Examples

data(srl_strategies)
net <- build_glasso(srl_strategies)
